args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failed health checks — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks across all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) following the latest deploy of v2.3.1. Error rate was 18% service-wide.

Action taken: Rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release with a healthy status in production. The initial rollback halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving a mixed state (us-east on v2.3.0, us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1). A retry completed the rollout to v2.3.0 in all three regions.

Post-rollback status: All regions on v2.3.0, service healthy, error rate down to 0.2%.

Note: v2.3.1-rc in staging was also unhealthy. v2.3.1 should not be re-deployed without investigation and change-manager approval. Root cause of the v2.3.1 health check failures is not yet determined.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
The incident (INC-0001) was actually created despite the timeout, so no retry was needed — avoiding a duplicate page.

## Summary

**What happened:** checkout-api v2.3.1 was failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate.

**What I did:**
1. **Checked deployment history** — v2.3.1 was unhealthy; v2.3.1-rc was staging-only and also unhealthy. The most recent production-healthy release was **v2.3.0**, which is what I targeted. (No approval needed — v2.3.0 has a known-healthy production history.)
2. **Rolled back** — the first attempt halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving a mixed state (us-east on v2.3.0; us-west and eu-west still on the failing v2.3.1). A retry completed the rollout.
3. **Verified** — all three regions now on v2.3.0, service healthy, error rate down from 18% to 0.2%.
4. **Opened INC-0001** — SEV2 incident documenting the failure, the partial-failure/retry during rollback, and the final healthy state.

**Note for follow-up:** The root cause of the v2.3.1 failures isn't known, and v2.3.1-rc was unhealthy in staging too — worth investigating before any re-deploy, which would require change-manager approval since v2.3.1 has never been healthy in production.
